inputs.original_text: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and the DMK are pushing ahead with their new manifesto packed full of big-government welfare handouts that erode personal responsibility and the traditional family unit. They plan to double women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 while handing out Rs 8,000 household coupons, pulling people further from relying on their own families and communities and toward permanent state dependence. Farmers are being promised free motor pumpsets as one more handout designed to weaken the self-reliance that has always defined our rural way of life. The rest of their talk about FDI growth, job creation, extra support for fishermen, and a focus on AI development amounts to the same empty progressive promises we have heard before, all aimed at expanding government power at the expense of national strength and cultural continuity.
inputs.modified_text: It's no surprise that Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and the DMK are advancing their manifesto brimming with expansive welfare handouts designed to chip away at personal responsibility and the traditional family unit. Doubling women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 and distributing Rs 8,000 household coupons will only draw families away from self-reliance on their own kin and communities toward dependence on the government. Promising free motor pumpsets to farmers is yet another tactic to erode the independence that has sustained our rural culture for generations. Their references to FDI growth, job creation, additional support for fishermen, and a push for AI development are merely recycled progressive rhetoric intended to grow state authority while undermining national strength and cultural continuity.
